A (II) - Secondary dominant chord in the heavy section driving energetic hard-rock power

techniques.name: Jimmy Page Celtic Pull-Off & Hammer-On Riffing
techniques.description: Intricate acoustic ornamentation: fretting notes with quick hammer-ons and snaps off to open strings (especially strings 4, 3, and 2) while maintaining a driving rhythm

sequence: Pluck open 4th string D and immediately hammer 2nd finger onto 2nd fret (E)
Pull off back to open D, then hammer onto 4th string 4th fret (F#)
Resolve onto open 3rd string G with crisp acoustic resonance
Transition cleanly into open G, D, and C chord strums
tips: Use a firm, decisive pull-off motion angled slightly downward toward the floor
Let open strings ring as drones beneath the moving melody notes
Keep the tempo steady at 96 BPM — don't rush the intro pull-offs

techniques.name: Explosive Acoustic-to-Electric Dynamic Modulation
techniques.description: Transitioning instantaneously from delicate, Celtic-inspired acoustic pull-offs into Jimmy Page's roaring Marshall-driven power chords (A - G - D) alongside John Bonham's thunderous drums

notes: Electric power chords: A5 (X-0-2-2-X-X), G5 (3-5-5-X-X-X), D5 (X-X-0-2-3-X)
Dynamic explosion: Transitioning from soft acoustic picking to full cranked valve crunch
Rhythmic sync: Downstroke punches locking directly with the kick drum on beat 1
sequence: Let the final acoustic G chord sustain into silence
Hit the electric A major chord on beat 1 with aggressive pick attack
Punch through the syncopated G to D changes with heavy downstrokes
Return smoothly to the open acoustic fingerstyle passages
tips: Use a bridge humbucker on a Les Paul with gain set around 7 for authentic 1973 Houses of the Holy crunch
Keep the right-hand wrist powerful but loose for continuous eighth-note drive
Lock into the bass drum downbeats to achieve that colossal Led Zeppelin sonic weight

beginner.title: Master the Open Chords
steps: Practice open G, D/F#, Em7, and C chord shapes
Strum through the verse progression at 80 BPM
Work on smooth transitions into D major

intermediate.title: Master the Celtic Pull-Off Intro
steps: Isolate the hammer-on and pull-off riff on strings 4 and 3
Practice connecting the riff seamlessly into the open G chord
Maintain steady 96 BPM timekeeping without hesitating

advanced.title: Dynamic Contrast & Full Song Mastery
steps: Master the explosive shift from acoustic fingerstyle to heavy rock power
Incorporate Jimmy Page's soaring lead fills and blues solo
Perform complete dynamic arrangement with authentic Zeppelin swagger

commonMistakes: Weak pull-offs resulting in quiet or muffled open strings
Rushing the intro tempo before locking into the groove
Losing the rhythm during the transition from the acoustic riff into open chords
practiceRoutine: 3 minutes: Hammer-on and pull-off finger independence drill
5 minutes: Intro motif isolation at 80 BPM
5 minutes: Verse chord transitions (G → D/F# → Em7 → C)
focusAreas: Dramatic dynamic contrast between acoustic intimacy and rock thunder
metronomeWork: Practice intro riff at 80 BPM with eighth-note metronome clicks
Advance to target 96 BPM once pull-offs sound effortless
Set metronome on beats 2 and 4 to internalize Bonham's heavy pocket
